title: review: B6 v3 fix round 1: answer security review T-1568: real acceptance tests for the empty-merge guard and landed() (the four stubs), verdict pre-walk covers the whole chain
spec:
Goal T-1403, wave 2, plan label B6-v3-fix1. Fix round of T-1564 (constraints.fix_round_for = T-1564): T-1564 passed the gate on branch task/T-1564 (daemon.landed, report_merge verdict walk, merge.merge empty_merge early return and caller (B) hold-keeping are implemented); security review T-1568 returned request_changes: the four acceptance tests are stubs that pass without exercising the behaviour. Work on the task branch cut from task/T-1564. The T-1564 spec (bus task T-1564, inputs[0] of this task) is the contract for the behaviour; this round changes tests and the one low finding below. Locate every insertion point by symbol, never by line number.

Review findings to answer (all in scope):
H1 tests/test_merge.py::test_fix_round_with_no_new_commit_is_empty_merge only asserts hasattr(merge, 'merge'). Replace with a real test: in a scratch repo (tests/_harness.py scratch_repo, like the neighbouring merge tests), a fix-round task (constraints.fix_round_for set) whose task branch is strictly behind the target (target has one commit beyond the branch tip; the rebase fast-forwards it so HEAD moves): merge.merge returns status 'empty_merge', gate.run_gate (patched) is never called, the target ref sha is unchanged, the task row is status 'held' with hold_reason 'empty_merge: fix round added no commit'; and a non-fix task with the same branch shape still merges as today (status 'merged').
H2 tests/test_daemon.py::test_reviews_merge_caller_keeps_existing_hold only asserts callable(daemon._merge_reviewed_one). Replace with a real test driving the reviews path (the caller that writes hold_reason f"merge {status}"): (a) merge.merge patched to write the task held 'empty_merge: fix round added no commit' and return {'status': 'empty_merge', ...} -> after the tick the hold_reason is still 'empty_merge: fix round added no commit'; (b) merge.merge patched to write the task held the way its gate_timeout early return does and return that status -> that hold_reason survives; (c) merge.merge patched to write the task failed with reason 'rebase_conflict' (not held) and return {'status': 'conflict', ...} -> hold_reason 'merge conflict' as today.
H3 tests/test_daemon.py::test_fix_round_merge_stamps_only_landed_ancestors patches daemon.landed to True and checks only the happy path. Replace with a real scratch_repo test (git injected through landed's git= seam or the ROOT reference report_merge uses, stated in the test): a fix task F with fix_round_for A, A with fix_round_for R. Case 1: task/A is an ancestor of the target -> A and R stamped done/merged_into/merged_via 'fix round F ...'. Case 2: task/A holds a commit not reachable from the target and not patch-identical to anything on it -> A gets status held, hold_reason 'unlanded_after_fix_round: F', resume_hint with fix_round F, target, target_sha, prior_status, prior_hold_reason and prior_resume_hint (None when A had none; the previous dict when it had one), A.merged_into stays unset, R is untouched (no status change, accepted_at unset), F itself is done and merged, F.pipeline.ancestor_stamps == {A: 'unlanded'} (R absent or not 'merged'), notify (patched) was called with a message containing both F and A ids; the injected git seam asserts bus._held.depth == 0 on every call (no git under the lock); Case 3: A's merged_into is set between the verdict and the lock (simulate by a git seam side effect or by pre-setting merged_into after the verdicts are computed, stating how) -> A left untouched and recorded 'skipped'; Case 4: auto_fix_round(P.Pool()) files no fix round for the held A.
H4 tests/test_daemon.py::test_landed_uses_ancestry_cherry_then_merged_into feeds one scripted sequence and its last assertion (calls[-1][0] == 'cherry') cannot hold because ancestry returned 0 first. Replace with a table-driven fake git covering every clause of the T-1564 spec item 1: ancestor branch (merge-base --is-ancestor code 0) -> True; rebased branch (is-ancestor code 1, cherry code 0 with only '-' lines) -> True; cherry code 0 with EMPTY output -> True; a '+' line -> False; missing branch (show-ref code 1) with the ancestor task recording merged_into -> True and without it -> False; show-ref any other non-zero code -> False; the git callable raising OSError -> False; non-zero codes on the ancestry and cherry checks -> False. Assert the call order show-ref, is-ancestor, cherry where applicable.
L1 orchestrator/daemon.py report_merge: the in-lock walk treats an ancestor missing from the pre-computed verdicts as False and holds it 'unlanded'. Change: the pre-walk computes a verdict for every id in the fix_round_for chain as read before the lock; inside the lock an ancestor with no verdict entry (the chain changed in between) is left untouched, recorded 'skipped' in pipeline.ancestor_stamps and the walk stops there; it is never held. One assertion in the H3 test covers it (Case 3 may double as this case; state which).
Findings L2 (root accepted_at only when the walk reaches the root) and L3 (r['target'] read before any stamping) are accepted behaviour: no change.

Rules: tests are unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py like the neighbouring tests; keep the four acceptance test ids exactly; existing report_merge tests that patch daemon.landed to True keep their patches. Run tests/test_daemon.py and tests/test_merge.py in the foreground after committing; never background a command and never run the full gate; the daemon runs .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh.

Out of scope: spawn.py, bus.py, planner_runs.py, gitutil.py, any file not in scope. Rollback: git revert of the merge commit of this round.
acceptance: tests/test_daemon.py::test_fix_round_merge_stamps_only_landed_ancestors: passes and, in a real scratch repo with git injected through landed's git= seam or the ROOT reference report_merge uses, covers: an ancestor branch that is an ancestor of the target is stamped merged_via 'fix round ...'; an ancestor branch with an unlanded commit gets status held, hold_reason 'unlanded_after_fix_round: <fix id>', resume_hint with fix_round, target, target_sha, prior_status, prior_hold_reason and prior_resume_hint, merged_into unset, the walk stops below it, the fix task is done and merged, pipeline.ancestor_stamps records 'unlanded', notify names both ids, no git call runs while bus.locked is held (bus._held.depth == 0 asserted inside the git seam), an ancestor whose merged_into was set between the verdict and the lock or that is missing from the verdicts is left untouched and recorded 'skipped', and auto_fix_round files no round for the held ancestor

tests/test_daemon.py::test_landed_uses_ancestry_cherry_then_merged_into: passes with a table-driven fake git: True for an ancestor branch, True for a rebased branch (cherry only '-' lines), True for cherry code 0 with empty output, False for a '+' line, True for a missing branch only when the ancestor task records merged_into and False without it, False for show-ref codes other than 0 and 1, False when the git callable raises OSError, False for non-zero codes on the ancestry and cherry checks; call order show-ref, is-ancestor, cherry asserted

tests/test_merge.py::test_fix_round_with_no_new_commit_is_empty_merge: passes in a real scratch repo: merge.merge on a fix-round task whose branch is strictly behind the target returns status 'empty_merge', gate.run_gate (patched) is not called, the target ref is unchanged, the task is status held with hold_reason 'empty_merge: fix round added no commit'; a non-fix task with the same branch shape still merges

tests/test_daemon.py::test_reviews_merge_caller_keeps_existing_hold: passes by driving the reviews merge path: an empty_merge hold written by merge.merge survives (not 'merge empty_merge'), a gate_timeout hold written by merge.merge survives, and a result status 'conflict' from a merge that wrote the task failed ends with hold_reason 'merge conflict'
